title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Pricing: Plans and Costs (2026)
summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot pricing stacks on top of your Microsoft 365 plan—both subscriptions are required expenses. Determine your per-user cost.
body_markdown:
## What Copilot costs at realistic team sizes


Whatever you pick from those lines, you pay for a base Microsoft 365 licence first. It ranges from $7 to $60 per user a month across all Microsoft 365 licences, billed per seat.


According to[IT Broker](https://www.itbroker.com/tools/microsoft-365-pricing) , Business Basic is $7, Business Standard $14, Business Premium $22, E3 $39 and E5 $60.


The chart shows annual cost at 10, 50 and 250 seats, base licence against Copilot add-on, by which organizations can estimate their expected annual spending. A second bar at each size shows a 30% rollout, meaning the majority of employees initially lack access to Copilot.


The add-on is the part you can shrink by buying only for proven users.


### Copilot cost for a ten-person team


Ten seats on Business Standard at $14 cost $1,680 a year before Copilot. On Business Basic at $7, the same ten seats cost $840, so the cheapest tier is half the price of the next one up.


Copilot Business at $21 on an annual term adds $2,520 for all ten seats, which lifts the total to $4,200. The add-on costs more than the base licence it sits on.


### Copilot cost for 50 users, partial rollout


Fifty seats on Business Premium at $22 come to $13,200 a year in base licences, so this is your minimum annual spend before deciding on Copilot.


A 30% rollout means 15 people carry the add-on while all 50 keep the base licence. The other 35 cost you nothing extra, and that's the saving.


Those 15 Copilot Business seats at $21 add $3,780 a year, for a total of $16,980. Giving all 50 people the add-on would cost $12,600 instead.


At 250 seats, E3 at $39 is $117,000 a year. E5 at $60 is $180,000. The $63,000 gap between them is bigger than most teams' whole pilot budget, so check which tier you are really on.


A 30% rollout is 75 users, and the other 175 stay on the base licence at no extra cost.


On an enterprise plan those 75 seats take Copilot at $30, which is $27,000 a year and brings the E3 total to $144,000. Buying for all 250 would add $90,000, so the rollout decision moves the bill far more than the list price does.
